# windows_ntp (Data Source)

Reads the current Windows Time service (W32Time) time-source state of the remote Windows host without managing it. This is a **singleton** data source — no lookup keys are required.

Exposes `type` (`NTP`/`NT5DS`/`AllSync`/`NoSync`), the ordered `servers` peer list (`address` plus `flags`), `special_poll_interval_seconds`, `reliable` (`AnnounceFlags` `5`), `ntp_server_enabled`, `max_pos_phase_correction_seconds` / `max_neg_phase_correction_seconds`, the informational `current_source` (`w32tm /query /source`, opaque peer name), `policy_override` and `domain_joined`.

The Terraform data source ID is the stable `machine_id` (HKLM MachineGuid).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Singleton — no lookup keys required.
data "windows_ntp" "current" {}

output "type" {
  value = data.windows_ntp.current.type
}

output "servers" {
  value = data.windows_ntp.current.servers
}

output "current_source" {
  value = data.windows_ntp.current.current_source
}

output "id" {
  value = data.windows_ntp.current.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `current_source` (String) Current time source as reported by `w32tm /query /source` (opaque peer name). Empty when the query fails.
- `domain_joined` (Boolean) Whether the host is joined to an Active Directory domain as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Data source ID; the stable machine ID (HKLM MachineGuid).
- `max_neg_phase_correction_seconds` (Number) Largest backward clock correction the service may apply, in seconds, as observed on the host.
- `max_pos_phase_correction_seconds` (Number) Largest forward clock correction the service may apply, in seconds, as observed on the host.
- `ntp_server_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the host answers NTP requests as observed on the host.
- `policy_override` (Boolean) Whether Group Policy carries `Type` or `NtpServer` for W32Time as observed on the host.
- `reliable` (Boolean) Whether the host is a reliable time source as observed on the host (`AnnounceFlags` `5`).
- `servers` (Attributes List) NTP peers as observed on the host, in order (`address` plus `flags`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--servers))
- `special_poll_interval_seconds` (Number) Poll interval in seconds as observed on the host.
- `type` (String) W32Time sync type as observed on the host (`NTP`, `NT5DS`, `AllSync` or `NoSync`).

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `servers`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) Peer hostname or address as observed on the host.
- `flags` (String) Per-peer flags as observed on the host (canonical lower-case hex, e.g. `0x9`).
